s1.brief: BALANCED HEAVY version: a wide, substantial angular S with the same broad side-ribbon mass as M. Keep the corners softly rolled like M and the center about two-thirds as thick as the sides. Preserve both open opposing S apertures.
s1.prompt: Create ONE HEAVY, WIDE uppercase S in our ORIGINAL M typeface style. Image 1 is the style master: copy its actual broad ribbon thickness, soft asymmetric joins and rounded-flat terminals. Image 2 gives ONLY the angular S skeleton; its thin pen weight must not influence the result. Match M at equal cap height: make both long outside diagonal ribbons very broad, around 25-30 percent of cap height. The middle connecting ribbon stays BOLD too, around 16-18 percent of cap height: only a little thinner than the outside, never a hairline. Make the whole S wider as needed to hold these thick ribbons and keep the open gaps. Follow the drawing's geometry: long straight upper-left and lower-right diagonals; a connecting middle bridge that gently rises left to right; a short downward upper-right return and a short upward lower-left return. Use M's compact soft corners and subtle taper on this strict angular structure. A heavy filled ribbon letter, not a narrow zigzag symbol, outline or thin traced sketch. One connected solid WHITE glyph on pure BLACK. Only the S, fully inside a square with clear margins, no text or decorations. BALANCED HEAVY version: a wide, substantial angular S with the same broad side-ribbon mass as M. Keep the corners softly rolled like M and the center about two-thirds as thick as the sides. Preserve both open opposing S apertures.
